narr: A stationary frontal boundary across central Minnesota, and an increasing very moist airmass with PWATs near 1.75 early Friday morning, July 15th, was the setup for a flash flood event over Chippewa County Wisconsin. During the early morning, several waves of thunderstorms developed across west central, Wisconsin, and east central Minnesota, and drifted southeast across west central Wisconsin for several hours. The upper level flow was conducive for training of the thunderstorms as a strong low level jet at 850H impinged upon very moist airmass. By daybreak, a pocket of 4 to 5 inches of rain fell in Chippewa County where flash flooding was reported. Elsewhere, rainfall totals ranged from 2 to 4 inches from Barron to Chippewa County.
ev: Local authorities reported closed roads due to flooding in the city of Stanley. In addition, several culverts were washed out and streams were running high between Stanley and Colburn. Based on the flash flood guidance, the rainfall totals were nearly two times that amount to flood. Radar estimates between Colburn and Stanley average between 4 and 6 inches, with an unofficial report of 5.40 inches in the city of Stanley.
